title: I vibe-coded a browser-based basketball player creator with NBA DNA blending — here's what I learned about directing AI
author: taggerungDC
selftext:
Hey,

Full disclosure up front: **I built this primarily through vibe coding with ChatGPT.** I designed the systems, UX flow, and attribute logic, then iterated with AI on implementation. This is a collaboration, not a solo hand-coding project — I want to be transparent about that.

**What it is:**

**Prospect Lab** — a character creator for building original Pokémon-inspired basketball players. The fantasy is drafting a star, customizing their identity and playstyle, then generating a pro-level dossier with stats that actually mean something.

**What it does:**

* Full creator: identity, appearance, personality, signature ability, backstory
* 13 archetypes (Floor General, Stretch Big, Lockdown Defender, etc.)
* "Plays Like" system — pick a real NBA player, their tendencies blend into your generated attributes
* 16 attributes on a 1-99 scale with **position-weighted OVR** (Centers value interior D/rebounding more than PGs)
* Species traits that flavor the build without hard-locking anything
* Auto-generated playstyle analysis based on the actual build
* Save/load via localStorage + randomizer that respects physical logic. Unfortunately, you will have to screenshot your finished prospects because I have not yet added exporting via JSON or a PNG.

**Play it:** [https://nikoprower.itch.io/prospect-lab](https://nikoprower.itch.io/prospect-lab)

**What directing AI taught me:**

* **Prompt architecture matters more than prompts.** I spent more time designing the data model and calculation pipeline than writing code snippets. The AI excelled at implementation once the logic was clear.
* **You still need to know what's wrong.** The first OVR formula averaged everything equally — I had to recognize why that broke the fantasy and redesign the position weights myself.
* **AI writes fast, but coherence is on you.** The randomizer generated 7'3" point guards with 99 speed until I added physical constraint rules.
* **Refactoring is the real work.** The first version had hardcoded logic everywhere. I had to direct the restructuring into modular data architecture for future expansion.

**What I'd love feedback on:**

* General Issues and feedback. Does the thing work well and if it doesn't what could I fix?
* Does the OVR weighting feel fair across positions?
* The playstyle analysis is rule-based — anyone experimented with procedural scouting report text?
* UX: does the creation flow feel like a sports RPG or still too form-heavy?
* For other vibe coders: what patterns have you found for keeping AI-generated code maintainable?
